title: Enforce SSHv2 and Strong Cryptographic Algorithms
description: Network management access must exclusively use SSH Version 2. Legacy SSH Version 1 and unencrypted cleartext remote management must be strictly disabled.
rationale: SSHv1 has critical vulnerabilities including session hijacking and CRC32 compensation attacks. SSHv2 provides robust message integrity and encryption.
failure_message: SSHv2 is not enforced. Either SSH is disabled or legacy SSHv1 is permitted.
warning_message: SSH is enabled but cipher suite strength is unverified.

title: Disable Insecure Telnet Protocol
description: The Telnet protocol transmits credentials and commands in cleartext across the network. Telnet server daemons and transport input must be disabled.
rationale: Cleartext transmission of administrative credentials enables trivial credential theft, man-in-the-middle attacks, and unauthorized device takeover.
failure_message: Telnet service is enabled on administrative management interfaces or VTY lines.

title: Disable Cleartext HTTP Web Management
description: Insecure HTTP web server management services must be disabled. Administrative web consoles must not accept unencrypted HTTP traffic.
rationale: Cleartext HTTP exposes web session cookies, administrative login credentials, and configuration payloads to network sniffing and eavesdropping.
failure_message: Cleartext HTTP server daemon is active and listening for management connections.

title: Enforce Secure HTTPS Web Management with TLS 1.2+
description: If web management is enabled, it must mandate HTTPS utilizing TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3 with secure cipher suites.
rationale: HTTPS encrypts management traffic, protecting integrity and confidentiality against interception.
failure_message: Secure HTTPS server daemon is not enabled for secure administrative web management.

title: Enforce SNMPv3 with AuthPriv and Disable Default Communities
description: Simple Network Management Protocol must utilize SNMPv3 with authentication and encryption (authPriv). Default community strings ('public', 'private') must be removed.
rationale: SNMPv1 and SNMPv2c transmit community strings in plaintext. Weak or default community strings allow unauthorized telemetry gathering or device reconfiguration.
failure_message: SNMPv3 with authPriv is not enforced or insecure default community strings (e.g. 'public') are present.
